football_evidence.question: Can Michigan contain Indiana’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Indiana, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 4.5 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Michigan has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Michigan’s offense has allowed a sack on 6.3% of its dropbacks, and Indiana’s defense sacks the quarterback on 11.5% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
When Michigan has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Michigan’s offense averages 4.9 yards per carry, and Indiana’s defense allows 3.7 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

When Michigan has the ball (big plays on the ground): Michigan’s offense turns 6.0% of its runs into explosive gains, and Indiana’s defense gives up explosive gains on 4.3% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
In his last two games (Minnesota and Penn State), Underwood averaged 4.5 yards per attempt, against 8.3 in his four games before that.
contradicting: When Indiana has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Indiana’s offense has allowed a sack on 5.4% of its dropbacks, and Michigan’s defense sacks the quarterback on 8.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Indiana has the ball (big plays on the ground): Indiana’s offense turns 8.6% of its runs into explosive gains, and Michigan’s defense gives up explosive gains on 1.2% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Indiana has the ball (early downs): Indiana’s offense succeeds on 42.0% of its first- and second-down plays, and Michigan’s defense allows success on 36.9% of first- and second-down plays (FBS average 42.7%).
When Indiana has the ball (the red zone): Indiana’s offense succeeds on 37.3% of its red-zone plays, and Michigan’s defense allows success on 29.3% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).
quarterbacks: Bryce Underwood has completed 72 of 126 passes (57.1%) for 924 yards, 7.3 yards per attempt, 5 touchdowns and 6 interceptions in six games for Michigan, and has been sacked on 8 of 134 dropbacks.
Josh Hoover has completed 108 of 168 passes (64.3%) for 1,661 yards, 9.9 yards per attempt, 18 touchdowns and no interceptions in seven games for Indiana, and has been sacked on 9 of 177 dropbacks.
Bryce Underwood does not appear on Michigan’s initial availability report.
Josh Hoover does not appear on Indiana’s initial availability report.
availability: Michigan’s availability report lists seven players as out, including offensive linemen Ace Hamilton and Andrew Sprague.
